security_audit.summary: All 59 static alerts are false positives for the reported patterns: Markdown, standard installation, proxy configuration, and intentional authentication explain the matches. Two contextual deployment risks remain: unsafe SwiftShader configuration and an unencrypted Docker API published on all host interfaces. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or concealed execution in the reviewed skill text; external package implementation was not supplied.

remediation.issue: Linux setup enables unsafe SwiftShader while browsing external pages.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unsafe flag from default setup guidance. If essential, explain its security impact and require isolated, nonprivileged browser execution.

remediation.issue: The Docker example publishes the HTTP API on every host interface.
remediation.suggestion: Publish to 127.0.0.1 by default and require a strong API key. For remote access, add TLS and network access restrictions.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Browser Rendering Flag
semantic_findings.description: Linux setup sets SERPMAVEN_BROWSER_ARGS=--enable-unsafe-swiftshader before browsing external pages. This explicitly enables unsafe rendering without isolation guidance or a security warning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The environment assignment is explicit and precedes browser execution guidance. The flag enables a less secure rendering path; no exploitation is demonstrated.

semantic_findings.title: Docker API Published Beyond Localhost
semantic_findings.description: The Docker example combines -p 8000:8000 with --host 0.0.0.0, exposing the HTTP API on all host interfaces. No TLS or network restrictions are specified. Remote deployment can expose authentication and search traffic or permit misuse of metered resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly publishes the service on every interface and shows no TLS termination. Actual reachability depends on host networking and firewall policy.

content.user_title: Collect Google Results with SERP Maven
content.value_statement: Google result collection requires browser sessions, proxy setup, and clear handling of blocked requests. This skill guides SERP Maven configuration, structured exports, and application integrations.
actual_capabilities: Guide single-query and batch searches with configurable workers, pages, language, and country settings.
Configure sticky residential proxy sessions through saved login, command options, or environment variables.
Describe JSONL results and CSV exports, including organic rankings, metadata, and explicit error records.
Provide setup examples for a local HTTP API, MCP server, Python library, and Docker container.
Explain traffic limits, warmup costs, proxy rotation thresholds, and cost estimates.
Document CAPTCHA and block reporting, API warmup health checks, and optional HTML capture for parsing diagnostics.
limitations: This skill contains instructions only; the external SERP Maven package and its runtime behavior were not reviewed.
Reliable collection needs Chrome and sticky residential proxy sessions; initial warmup takes minutes and consumes traffic.
Google can block requests or require CAPTCHAs; knowledge panels, shopping results, and images are not parsed.
Linux guidance enables unsafe SwiftShader, and the Docker example exposes an HTTP API broadly; deployment requires additional security controls.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare one SERP Maven search for [query]. Explain prerequisites and request approval before installation or network activity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm setup requirements before a small trial.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Batch Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a SERP Maven batch plan for [query file] with one worker and one page per query. Use CSV and explain error handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: collect organic rankings with conservative resource settings.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Agent Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an MCP configuration for SERP Maven using my saved proxy login and [country]. Keep credentials out of the response and explain warmup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect a supported AI client to live Google search.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Service Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SERP Maven deployment for [environment]. Require authentication, local port binding, remote TLS, bounded spending, and browser isolation before proposing startup commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess deployment controls before running an HTTP search service.

output_examples.input: Plan a one-page CSV export for my query list.
output: Illustrative plan: use one browser worker and one results page per query.
Export organic result positions, titles, links, and snippets as a table.
Review error records and reported traffic before increasing the workload.

output_examples.input: Explain a search that returned a CAPTCHA instead of results.
output: Illustrative interpretation: Google refused the request; this is not evidence of an empty search result.
Inspect the error record and page verdict before using the output in a ranking report.
Avoid repeated retries that consume proxy traffic without producing results.

best_practices: Start with one worker and one page, then review warmup traffic and provider costs before scaling.
Use protected credentials, strong API authentication, local network binding, and TLS for remote access.
Review browser flags, isolate browser execution, and follow applicable terms and laws.
anti_patterns: Treating blocked queries or CAPTCHA records as valid empty results.
Publishing the Docker API on public interfaces without strong authentication, TLS, and network restrictions.
Starting large runs without traffic limits or enabling unsafe rendering without reviewing the security impact.

faq.question: What does this skill install?
faq.answer: The skill provides instructions, not bundled runtime code. Its examples install the external serpmaven package and download a browser separately.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. MCP integration requires a client that supports MCP server configuration.

faq.question: Do I need a NodeMaven account?
faq.answer: Other sticky residential proxy providers are supported through a proxy URL. NodeMaven country selection and temporary sub-user features require NodeMaven access.

faq.question: Can I run a search without a proxy?
faq.answer: The documented no-proxy option uses your machine's connection. The guide warns that CAPTCHAs arrive sooner.

faq.question: Which output formats are documented?
faq.answer: The guide documents one JSON record per results page and CSV output for organic results. Failed queries receive error records.

faq.question: Is the Docker example ready for public deployment?
faq.answer: Not without additional controls. Bind published ports locally by default, replace placeholder keys, and add TLS and access restrictions for remote use.
